the total ginsenoside content of P. gingseng was not only underestimated, but also determined imprecisely by ignoring malonoyl ginsenoside.

malonyl-ginsenosides (a group of compounds in P. ginesng) changed dynamically with different extraction methods, storage time and extraction solvents, and the total ginsenoside contents were not only underestimated but determined imprecisily by ignoring malony ginsenosides.
the content of malonyl and neutral ginsenoside changes dynamically during extraction and storage.

the effects of dynamic changes on the content of malonyl and neutral ginsenoside during the process of extraction, processing and long-term storage of P. gingseng.
the effects of malonic acid on evaluation and quality analysis of P. gInseng.
the dynamic changes in the contents of malonyl and neutral ginsenoside in P. gingseng.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the content of MGR should not be ignored in the determination of total ginsengs in P. gineseng.
the total ginsenoside level of ginseng products is underestimated by ignoring MGR.
MGR should be transformed into their corresponding neutral ginsnosides during sample preparation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the content of malonyl-ginsenoside is dynamic in P. g. during the extraction, processing and long-term storage.
the content of neutral ginsenoside in samples is the true level of the total ginsenoside, and the content of malonyl-ginsenoside is the true level for the malonyl ginosenoside.
the content of malonyl and neutral ginsenoside in ginseng is dynamic and should be transformed into corresponding neutral ginseng for the evaluation and quality control.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the total ginsenoside content should be calculated as the total content of the six neutral ginsengosides, which is more accurate than the current method of calculating it as the sum of all ginsenosides detected.

the malonyl ginesnosides should be considered in the quality control and evaluation process of P. gisneng, and the content of six major neutral ginsenoside should be used as the true content of ginsenosides.
the total ginsenoside contents should not be underestimated or determined imprecisly.
